title: Browser RPA con Playwright

Solarized Website Content Comprehension Auditor & Rewriter

prior_audit.method: Direct fetch of audit/lessons-only/sections/S23.json returned 404 before creation.

learner_entry_state.credit_rule: Only prior concepts adjudicated USABLE count as learned.
learner_entry_state.critical_dependency_warning: S21 and S22 remain REPAIR_REQUIRED. S23 cannot assume the report package is reconciled, the email draft is safely approved, or the approval is bound to exact content/recipients merely because prior sections emitted labels or in-memory states.
usable: draft-only and human-handoff as product boundaries
API/export should be considered before UI automation
human approval must remain separate from automated generation
not_creditable: S22 recipient set was individually confirmed
S22 draft hash/idempotency guarantee is trustworthy
S21 package metrics and artifact hashes are reconciled
S22 sandbox addresses are safely non-routable

roadmap_expectation.T1: Navegación: DOM y locators orientados a usuario; auto-waiting y assertions
roadmap_expectation.T2: Flujos: formularios, uploads/downloads y sesiones; auth, estados y Page Objects
roadmap_expectation.T3: Diagnóstico: trace, screenshot y logs; selectores robustos, retries y recovery
roadmap_expectation.T4: Límites: API/export primero; términos, CAPTCHA, desktop fallback y handoff humano
roadmap_expectation.gate: robot contra sitio de prueba controlado, con trace de éxito/falla, download verificado y reanudación idempotente

live_site.evidence: Public text surface exposes Section 23 'Playwright RPA' and the canonical tagline. The hydrated theory body is not exposed by the text fetch, so render-only defects were not invented.

checks: The custom get_by_role model silently returns the first of two identical role/name matches instead of enforcing Playwright-style uniqueness.
The fake timeout loop advances a 500ms timeout clock to 600ms on the never-ready path.
The T2-A download fixture simply returns the same bytes placed into the in-memory upload store and never compares against an expected artifact digest.
The T3-A evidence helper returns trace/screenshot path strings but creates neither file.
run_with_retry accepts fn but never calls it; a scripted [timeout, None] sequence reports success while fn_called remains empty.

external_research.finding: User-facing locators are recommended; click actionability requires a locator to resolve to exactly one element; role locators do not substitute for accessibility audits.
Downloads live in a temporary context-owned directory and are deleted when the browser context closes; save_as persists them. download.failure and suggested_filename support stronger verification.
storage_state may contain sensitive cookies/headers capable of impersonation and should be kept out of repositories.
Real traces require tracing start/stop and can include screenshots, DOM snapshots and network activity; path strings are not evidence.
ElementHandle use is discouraged; Locators re-resolve up-to-date DOM elements for each action.
APIRequestContext can validate server-side postconditions after browser actions, useful for side-effect-safe recovery.

findings.evidence: Opening/reference treat the S21 report and S22 human-approved draft as established inputs.
findings.attack: S21/S22 remain REPAIR_REQUIRED; those artifacts and approval bindings are not creditable.
findings.defense: The curriculum needs continuity across sections.
findings.impact: Browser automation can operationalize a stale or unverified payload.
findings.repair: Require a validated persisted S21/S22 handoff object and recheck its hashes/state before any downstream browser action.

findings.evidence: Reference says S22 already left an approved email draft, then S23 obtains the report from the practice site.
findings.attack: If S23 obtains new report data after approval, the S22 draft approval is stale unless the new report is explicitly unrelated.
findings.defense: S23 may be intended as a separate adapter exercise.
findings.impact: Learner is taught an unsafe ordering of evidence acquisition and human approval.
findings.repair: State whether S23 is an independent new run; otherwise fetch/verify first, regenerate the draft, then require fresh approval.

findings.evidence: The only real Playwright block is explicitly a non-executed sketch; graded/theory examples primarily use dict models.
findings.attack: The roadmap gate promises a robot against a controlled test site with real trace/download evidence.
findings.defense: Dict models improve portability and conceptual isolation.
findings.impact: A learner can pass the theory without demonstrating Playwright behavior at all.
findings.repair: Include one minimal controlled local web fixture and execute the end-to-end Playwright contract in theory/lab evidence.

findings.evidence: playwright_sketch.py calls download.path(), closes browser, then returns that path.
findings.attack: Playwright deletes context-owned temporary downloads when the context closes; remote connections may not support path().
findings.defense: The sketch only illustrates API shape.
findings.impact: Canonical example can return a path to a file that no longer exists.
findings.repair: Persist with download.save_as() before closing the context and return the persisted path.

findings.evidence: The real sketch never checks download.failure(), suggested filename, size, expected hash or saved bytes.
findings.attack: The gate says download verificado, not merely download observed.
findings.defense: T2-A later discusses hashes conceptually.
findings.impact: The real Playwright path fails the section's own definition of success.
findings.repair: save_as, inspect failure/filename, compute full SHA-256, parse/validate expected content and record provenance.

findings.evidence: Custom get_by_role returns hits[0] when multiple role/name matches exist.
findings.attack: Playwright locator actions require a unique target; ambiguity should fail rather than select the first node.
findings.defense: The fixture contains one matching button in the happy path.
findings.impact: The model teaches a silent wrong-click failure mode Playwright is designed to reject.
findings.repair: Require len(hits)==1 and add zero-match and multi-match negative fixtures.

findings.evidence: Theory/callout use the equation 'accesibilidad = estabilidad'.
findings.attack: Role locators often improve resilience but do not prove accessibility; accessible names can also change.
findings.defense: The mnemonic encourages user-facing selectors.
findings.impact: Conflates test resilience with accessibility conformance.
findings.repair: Say user-facing locators often improve resilience and provide accessibility feedback, but do not replace accessibility testing.

findings.evidence: A universal role→label→testid→text→CSS order is prescribed.
findings.attack: Playwright recommends user-facing attributes and explicit contracts; test IDs may be the most resilient even though they are not user-facing.
findings.defense: A default heuristic reduces novice choice overload.
findings.impact: Learner may reject a better explicit test contract because it appears lower in a rigid ranking.
findings.repair: Teach two goals: user-visible semantics when behavior matters; explicit test ID when stable product contract is the goal; CSS/XPath last.

findings.evidence: wait_until uses while waited <= timeout and advances before exit; 500ms timeout reaches fake clock 600ms on never-ready path.
findings.attack: The simulation misrepresents timeout boundaries and models only one predicate, not Playwright actionability/auto-retrying assertions.
findings.defense: It is intended as a simplified polling analogy.
findings.impact: The simplified model becomes technically incorrect at the boundary learners are meant to reason about.
findings.repair: Use deadline-based polling and explicitly distinguish custom business readiness from built-in actionability and web-first assertions.

findings.evidence: T1-B says timeout should attach trace, but its code has no timeout evidence path and no negative fixture.
findings.attack: The diagnostic behavior is asserted rather than demonstrated.
findings.defense: Tracing is covered later in T3-A.
findings.impact: Learner sees a success-only waiting example while the text claims robust failure evidence.
findings.repair: Add a timeout fixture that produces a real trace/evidence record consumed by T3-A.

findings.evidence: T2-A upload stores bytes under plantilla.xlsx; download reads those exact same bytes back under the same name.
findings.attack: This models an echo, not a portal-generated export, and never compares the digest against an independent expected value.
findings.defense: It demonstrates byte hashing mechanics.
findings.impact: The example can never catch the central failure: exporting the wrong report.
findings.repair: Separate upload input from generated output bytes and compare the persisted output against an independently defined expected contract.

findings.evidence: Theory truncates SHA-256 to 12 hex characters for a verification artifact.
findings.attack: A display prefix can be convenient, but a verification/provenance identity should retain the full digest.
findings.defense: The fixture is synthetic and small.
findings.impact: Teaches a display identifier as though it were the integrity value.
findings.repair: Store full SHA-256; optionally display a short prefix separately.

findings.evidence: storage_state reuse is taught without warning that the state itself may contain impersonation-capable cookies/headers.
findings.attack: Playwright explicitly warns not to commit auth state and recommends a gitignored auth directory.
findings.defense: The lab uses demo credentials.
findings.impact: Learners can transfer the pattern to real portals and accidentally leak session credentials.
findings.repair: Teach storage_state as a secret-bearing artifact: gitignore, least-privilege test account, expiry, restricted retention and no logging.

findings.evidence: The Page Object example wraps a dict auth state but contains no Playwright Page or locator to centralize.
findings.attack: It does not demonstrate the maintenance benefit described in the paragraph.
findings.defense: The lab intentionally models behavior without Chromium.
findings.impact: A novice can leave without seeing what a Playwright Page Object actually encapsulates.
findings.repair: Add a minimal real PO wrapping Page and locators while retaining the dict model as a conceptual precursor.

findings.evidence: on_failure returns traces/{step}.zip and shots/{step}.png strings but creates neither artifact.
findings.attack: The callout/gate require openable trace evidence; a path string is not a trace.
findings.defense: The lab models package keys.
findings.impact: Another analyst cannot reproduce the failure despite the lesson claiming they can.
findings.repair: Generate trace and screenshot in the controlled Playwright run, then assert existence/nonzero size and attach hashes.

findings.evidence: Prose says filter console logs by ERR; code stores console[-3:] unfiltered.
findings.attack: The claimed signal-to-noise policy is not implemented.
findings.defense: The sample list is only three messages.
findings.impact: Learner receives conflicting instructions about diagnostic packaging.
findings.repair: Implement structured severity filtering while preserving a bounded context window around the error.

findings.evidence: Theory says never PII in screenshots/logs, but tracing can capture DOM snapshots and network activity and no redaction/retention mechanism is shown.
findings.attack: A trace may expose more sensitive material than a screenshot; a prose prohibition does not sanitize it.
findings.defense: The lab is synthetic.
findings.impact: Operational transfer can turn diagnostic evidence into a data-leak artifact.
findings.repair: Use synthetic/test accounts, define trace retention/access, block or redact sensitive fields/routes, and forbid production PII in training fixtures.

findings.evidence: Recovery teaches err=='stale' and reobtaining a locator after re-render as a classic failure mode.
findings.attack: Playwright Locators already resolve an up-to-date element on each action; ElementHandle use is discouraged and is the stale-object mental model.
findings.defense: Renavigation can still be necessary when business state is invalid.
findings.impact: Imports a Selenium/ElementHandle recovery model into a locator-first Playwright lesson.
findings.repair: Teach locator re-resolution as the default; reserve explicit recovery for page/business-state invalidation, not ordinary DOM replacement.

findings.evidence: run_with_retry(fn, errors, ...) never calls fn; it consumes a pre-scripted error list.
findings.attack: The function name and prose claim action retry/recovery, but no action is executed.
findings.defense: The list is a deterministic teaching fixture.
findings.impact: Success can be reported even when the supplied operation was never invoked.
findings.repair: Call the operation per attempt via a deterministic fake that raises typed errors, then record attempts and postconditions.

findings.evidence: should_retry marks all timeout/network/429 kinds retryable without knowing the operation or whether a side effect already occurred.
findings.attack: A timeout after a successful server-side action can duplicate an export/submit; 429 should obey Retry-After/backoff where applicable.
findings.defense: The prose later acknowledges idempotence windows and business keys.
findings.impact: The executable policy contradicts the strongest safety insight in the paragraph.
findings.repair: Classify retryability by error plus operation semantics; check server-side postcondition/idempotency key before repeating and honor provider backoff.

findings.evidence: Learning outcome and prose require checkpoint reanudación; the theory code implements no checkpoint or persisted last_ok_step.
findings.attack: A central T3 competency exists only as prose.
findings.defense: The paragraph explains the conceptual hazard unusually well.
findings.impact: Learner cannot test the crash window the section explicitly identifies.
findings.repair: Add a persisted checkpoint fixture with a crash-after-effect-before-checkpoint negative test and an idempotent server-side key.

findings.evidence: choose_integration selects API/export/RPA from booleans only and does not emit the reason/runbook evidence promised in prose.
findings.attack: Availability alone does not prove the API/export is authorized, fresh, equivalent to the required report or contractually allowed.
findings.defense: The hierarchy is a useful default bias away from brittle UI automation.
findings.impact: The robot can choose the wrong integration while claiming API-first correctness.
findings.repair: Evaluate equivalence, authorization, freshness, provider policy and auditability, then persist method+reason+evidence.

findings.evidence: Callout says every RPA flow should have a ticket to replace it with API when an API exists.
findings.attack: An API may exist but not expose equivalent or authorized functionality.
findings.defense: It pushes teams toward lower-fragility integrations.
findings.impact: Turns a preference into a universal architectural mandate.
findings.repair: Create a replacement ticket only when an API/export path is demonstrably equivalent and allowed.

findings.evidence: T4-B prose requires minimal url/step/screenshot payload; handle_blockers returns only action/reason/queue.
findings.attack: The human cannot resume from the promised context.
findings.defense: The code demonstrates blocker priority correctly: ToS before CAPTCHA.
findings.impact: Handoff is a label, not an actionable continuation packet.
findings.repair: Return run_id, safe URL, step, screenshot/trace references, last verified checkpoint and allowed next actions.

findings.evidence: Theory examples emit isolated dicts/prints without one persisted audit chain linking S21 payload, S22 draft/approval and S23 browser action.
findings.attack: The campaign handoff explicitly requires a persisted lineage; browser automation is the highest-risk place to break it.
findings.defense: Individual subtopics intentionally isolate concepts.
findings.impact: A later reviewer cannot prove which approved payload drove which browser run/download.
findings.repair: Carry run_id and immutable hashes through every event and write an append-only browser-action manifest.

findings.evidence: Dense unexplained or weakly glossed terms include locator, testid, layout, readiness, step, storage_state, Page Object, trace, on-call, flake, runner, stale, checkpoint, runbook, fallback, ToS and handoff.
findings.attack: ZERO_TECH learners must infer many operational concepts from English jargon rather than content.
findings.defense: API identifiers such as get_by_role and storage_state must remain literal.
findings.impact: Extraneous cognitive load obscures the actual control logic.
findings.repair: Introduce Spanish concept first with the API term in parentheses, then use a consistent vocabulary.

rejected_hypotheses: REJECTED: all CSS selectors are invalid; Playwright supports CSS/XPath but recommends them only as a last resort when more resilient contracts are unavailable.
REJECTED: test IDs are inherently worse than role locators; Playwright documents test IDs as highly resilient explicit contracts, though they are not user-facing.
REJECTED: storage_state reuse is inherently unsafe; Playwright explicitly supports it, but the saved state must be treated as sensitive.
REJECTED: all retries are bad; selective transient retries are valid when the operation is safe/idempotent and retry policy respects provider semantics.
REJECTED: Page Objects are an anti-pattern; Playwright documents POM as a valid structuring approach for larger suites.
REJECTED: CAPTCHA human handoff and ToS abort are defects; those are responsible boundaries and should be retained.
REJECTED: traces should always be enabled for every success; Playwright warns full tracing is performance-heavy and commonly recommends targeted/first-retry tracing.

meta_leak.source_only_text: Filename/id pre-V3 warning and the comment about agent diagrams.
meta_leak.reason: Confirmed only as TypeScript comments; the public text surface did not expose the hydrated lesson body.

priority_order: F03/F04/F05/F11/F15: make the gate real—controlled Playwright run, persistent verified download and actual traces.
F19/F20/F21: rebuild retry/recovery around executed operations, side-effect safety and persisted checkpoints.
F01/F02/F25: restore cross-section causal order and provenance from S21/S22 into browser actions.
F06/F09/F10/F18: correct Playwright locator/auto-wait/re-render mental models.
F13/F17: treat auth state and traces as sensitive artifacts.
F22/F24: make integration choice and handoff evidence actionable and persisted.
F07/F08/F12/F14/F16/F23/F26: repair precision, pedagogy and redaction.

USABLE: Prefer user-facing locators and explicit test contracts over brittle DOM chains.
Playwright actionability and web-first assertions reduce fixed-sleep races.
CAPTCHA is a stop/human-handoff condition, not a retry target.
ToS prohibition is an abort condition.
API/export-first is a useful bias when the alternative is equivalent and authorized.
Checkpoint alone is not idempotency; crash windows around side effects matter.
MISCONCEPTION_RISK: first matching node is a safe locator result
a returned trace path means a trace exists
stale handles are a normal locator-first Playwright recovery model
API availability alone means API should be selected
S22 approved draft can remain valid after S23 obtains new report data
